question: What is the primary purpose of removing sutures after a wound has healed?

options.A: To restart the bleeding process for better healing
options.B: To prevent foreign body inflammation and scarring
options.C: To measure the exact depth of the subcutaneous tissue
options.D: To allow the application of topical antibiotics

explanation: Leaving thread in the skin too long causes unnecessary local irritation, inflammation, and permanent marks across the scar line. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h1)

question: Why do sutures need to be taken out instead of left inside the body permanently?

options.A: Skin cells will permanently grow over the thread and trap it in bone.
options.B: Non-absorbable threads act as foreign objects that can trigger infection.
options.C: The body will naturally dissolve all types of suture material within a week.
options.D: Permanent synthetic threads interfere with normal skin sensation forever.

explanation: Non-absorbable materials do not break down inside the body and will cause chronic irritation or abscess formation if left indefinitely. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h1)

question: Which body area generally requires the earliest suture removal due to a rich blood supply?
explanation: Facial skin heals very fast because of abundant blood circulation, so sutures are removed early to avoid permanent track marks. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h2)

question: A patient had surgery on their knee joint two days ago. When should the nurse expect these sutures to be removed?
explanation: Joint areas experience constant pulling and stretching, requiring a longer healing time and delayed suture removal to prevent reopening. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h2)

question: What should a nurse do if they inspect a wound and notice the edges are still gaping apart?

options.A: Stop the procedure and notify the medical doctor.
options.B: Irrigate the open area with normal saline and remove them anyway.
options.C: Apply strong adhesive tape across the gap and pull the rest.
options.D: Proceed with removing half of the sutures carefully.

explanation: Gaping edges mean the wound has not healed properly, and removing the support will cause the incision to open completely. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h3)

question: Which health condition can significantly delay the normal wound healing process?
explanation: High blood sugar impairs circulation and white blood cell function, which slows down tissue repair and delays safe suture removal. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h3)

question: What specific tool is commonly used to snip skin threads during suture removal?
explanation: Specialized scissors or small curved blades are designed with a tiny hook to slide under the tight thread safely without cutting the skin. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h4)

question: Why must the skin around the incision be cleansed with an antiseptic before cutting the threads?

options.A: To numb the local skin nerve endings completely
options.B: To dissolve the remaining knot so scissors are not needed
options.C: To remove surface bacteria and prevent deep infection
options.D: To stain the thread so it is easier to see

explanation: Cleansing eliminates germs sitting on the skin surface, ensuring they do not enter the tiny tract when the thread is pulled through. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h4)

question: When pulling a cut interrupted suture out of the skin, which direction should the nurse pull the thread?

options.B: Straight down into the subcutaneous fat
options.D: Toward the opposite side of the wound

explanation: Pulling the thread away from the incision prevents the exposed, germ-carrying part of the thread from dragging through the delicate healing tissue. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h5)

question: What is the correct way to handle a continuous (running) suture during removal?

options.A: Cut the knot and pull the main strand so the loops slide out.
options.B: Cut every single loop in half and pull them all out sideways.
options.C: Leave the knots intact and push them deeper under the skin.
options.D: Unravel the entire line manually without using any scissors.

explanation: Continuous sutures are linked together as a single chain, so cutting the proper segments allows the whole strand to glide out smoothly. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h5)

question: What should the nurse apply across the incision after removing sutures to provide extra support?
explanation: Adhesive closure strips help hold the skin edges together gently while the deeper layers continue gaining strength after suture removal. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h6)

question: Why is it important to carefully inspect the removed threads and the incision site?

options.A: To ensure no small pieces of thread were left inside the skin
options.B: To count the exact number of stitches for insurance records
options.C: To prove to the patient that the procedure is finished
options.D: To save the old thread pieces for laboratory testing

explanation: Retained suture fragments act as foreign bodies that can trigger a delayed local infection or inflammatory reaction inside the tissue. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h6)

question: What is wound dehiscence?

options.A: The total numbness of nerves near the surgical site
options.B: The normal darkening of skin color around a healing cut
options.C: The rapid growth of new hair follicles over a scar
options.D: The partial or complete opening of a wound incision

explanation: Dehiscence happens when the edges of a healing wound separate and pull apart, requiring immediate medical attention. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h7)

question: Which symptom is most characteristic of a localized infection following suture removal?

options.A: Mild itching around the adhesive strips
options.B: Temporary skin numbness near the cut
options.C: Pus drainage and spreading skin warmth
options.D: Fading pink color of the scar line

explanation: Pus and warmth indicate bacterial multiplication and active inflammation, which signal that the wound is becoming infected. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h7)
